## Why the change is correct

- **The trigger's threshold is the active chain's.** `useSpaceSafeSelectorItems.ts:96-106` puts the current chain first when it builds a multi-chain item. For the current safe, it takes the threshold and owner count from `useSafeInfo()`, which is the active chain's Safe. `selectedChainId` is the item's first chain (`useSafeSelectorState.ts:37`), so it is the active chain too. Showing `selectedItem.threshold` as "N/M" is therefore accurate.
- **Removing the "is this safe multi-chain?" check is safe.** `isTriggerSafeMultiChain` only fed the `iconOnly` prop that this change drops. `sameAddress` has no other use in `index.tsx`. No other caller passes `isMultiChain`.
- **The Cypress checks now match.** `cypress/e2e/pages/safe_navigation.pages.js:75` and `spaces.page.js:434` already expect `N/M` text in the trigger badge.
- **The dropdown rows are unchanged.** Multi-chain rows (`MultiChainSafeItemRow`, `SafeRowStats`) keep their icon-only badge, and their tests still assert that.
- **The updated test catches a revert.** The default test item spans two chains, so restoring `iconOnly={… chains.length > 1}` would make the `2/3` assertion fail.

## Worth a look (P3, optional)

| # | Area | Where | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Testing | `apps/web/src/features/spaces/components/SafeSelectorDropdown/components/__tests__/SafeSelectorTriggerContent.test.tsx:147` | The test is titled "shows the active chain threshold", but it only sets the item-level numbers and leaves the per-chain `threshold`/`owners` empty. It would not notice if the trigger started reading `chains[n].threshold` instead of the item-level value. Suggestion: give the per-chain entries different values (e.g. `3/5`) and assert that `2/3` still shows. |
| 2 | Conventions | `apps/web/src/features/spaces/components/SafeSelectorDropdown/components/SafeSelectorTriggerContent.tsx:83-84` | AGENTS.md treats comments as tech debt. This two-line comment explains why the trigger differs from the icon-only dropdown summary, which is a real reason. It could be cut to one line or moved into the test name. Keeping it is fine. |

## Ruled out

- **An old threshold flashing during a chain switch** (`useSpaceSafeSelectorItems.ts:42`). Switching to another chain of the same Safe could, in principle, briefly show the previous chain's `N/M`. `useLoadSafeInfo` drops the cached Safe when the chain changes, and the store then falls back to `defaultSafeInfo`, which has no owners, so the badge hides. At most one render frame is exposed, so I did not file it.

- None of the nine review areas found a security, regression, performance, architecture or duplication issue.
- I ran the review areas myself instead of starting one agent per area, because the diff is 35 lines.
- The paired validate/refute agents did not run, so adjudicated 0 of 2.
- The "worth tidying" cleanup proposals and the last-run comparison were skipped.
- As you asked, I didn't run tests, lint or type-check, didn't modify any files, and didn't post anything.
